after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-7 \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & -7 \\ 4 & 1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -7 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -7 \\ 0 & 3 & -15 \\ 4 & 1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -7 \\ 0 & 3 & -15 \\ 0 & 5 & k-28\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 5 & k-28\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & k-3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k-3.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k-3\,⇒\,k=3.
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,4,-5⟩$, $c=⟨3,-9,15⟩$, and  $u=⟨2,-2,11⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
after.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ 15\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+3t=2 \\ 4s-9t=-2 \\ -5s+15t=11\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 4 & -9 & -2 \\ -5 & 15 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ -5 & 15 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=1,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $s$ and $t$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc=u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $u$ does *not* lie on the plane $Π.$

content.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,4,-5⟩$, $c=⟨3,-9,15⟩$, and  $u=⟨2,-2,11⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
content.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ 15\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+3t=2 \\ 4s-9t=-2 \\ -5s+15t=11\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 4 & -9 & -2 \\ -5 & 15 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ -5 & 15 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=1,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $s$ and $t$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc=u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $u$ does *not* lie on the plane $Π.$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨1,2,3⟩$, $c=⟨3,8,-7⟩$, and  $u=⟨9,22,-5⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
after.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 22 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s+3t=9 \\ 2s+8t=22 \\ 3s-7t=-5\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 8 & 22 \\ 3 & -7 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 3 & -7 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -16 & -32\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+8{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}s+3t=9 \\ 2t=4 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
2t=4\,⟹\,t=2.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s+3t & =9 \\ s+3(2) & =9 \\ s & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=3,\,t=2,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=3b+2c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=3\cdot 2=6.$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ 4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=8 \\ -3{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}=-7 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 8 \\ -3 & 7 & -7 \\ -2 & 4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & 7 & -7 \\ -2 & 4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ -2 & 4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & k+8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k+8.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k+8\,⇒\,k=-8.
$$

content.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ 4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=8 \\ -3{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}=-7 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 8 \\ -3 & 7 & -7 \\ -2 & 4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & 7 & -7 \\ -2 & 4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ -2 & 4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & k+8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k+8.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k+8\,⇒\,k=-8.
$$
